LESSON: PEACE AND NON - VIOLENT CONFLICT RESOLUTION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Relationships
Topic 3.6: Peace and Non - violent Conflict Resolution
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Peace and Non - violent Conflict Resolution, part of People, Population and Relationships in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can resolving conflicts help us live peacefully in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Peace and Non - violent Conflict Resolution together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Peace: learners enhance the skill of resolving differences as they research online on peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family.

Unity: learners display team spirit as they work in groups to compose poems on the importance of peace in the family and present in class

Love: learners’ empathy is enhanced as they watch signed audio visual clips on various ways of empathizing with victims of conflict.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: learners work together harmoniously when role-playing peace-building scenarios.

Link to other Subjects:

English, Kiswahili and Kenya Sign Language: learners apply language skills when discussing and presenting on situations that may lead to

conflicts.

Suggested Learning resources:

digital devices, print resources and approved textbooks, signed audio visual clips,
